Performers
Münchener Bach-⁠Chor (chorus (Chorus I and II)), Münchener Chorknaben (boys’ choir, ripieno soprano (chorale ‘O Lamm Gottes, unschuldig’)), Münchener Bach-⁠Orchester (orchestra), Karl Richter (conductor) Documented

The booklet track list gives the chorale to the Knabenchor. The booklet also names instrumental soloists for the whole Passion (flutes Walther Theurer and Wolfgang Haag; oboes Edgar Shann and Kurt Hausmann; organ Ekkehard Tietze and Hedwig Bilgram; double bass Franz Ortner; bassoon Karl Kolbinger; viola da gamba Oswald Uhl), and Fritz Rothschuh as chorus master. Their assignment to this number is not stated, so they are not listed as performers of it.

[3] [6] [5]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition is not identified. The booklet gives the composition as Leipzig 1729 or earlier, revised 1736, and cites the autograph score Mus. ms. Bach P 25 and the parts St 110. The booklet and the Bach-⁠Gesellschaft score number this chorus No. 1; the New Bach Edition also numbers it 1.

[3] [2]
Recorded
23 June – 21 August 1958 (sessions 23 June–6 July, 11–⁠12 August and 21 August) Documented

The Archiv Produktion LP labels print the recording dates as 6/23–⁠7/6, 8/11–⁠12 and 21/1958; the retail page gives 23 June–6 July, 11–⁠12 and 21 August 1958; the booklet essay gives 22 sessions between 23 June and 21 August 1958 and its credit line gives 6–⁠8/1958. Which session produced No. 1 is not stated.

[6] [4] [3]
Place
Herkulessaal, Munich Documented

The booklet credit reads ‘München, Herkules-⁠Saal’.

[3] [4]
Label
Archiv Produktion (Deutsche Grammophon Gesellschaft, History of Music Division) Documented

The labels read ‘Archive Production — History of Music Division Deutsche Grammophon Ges.’ and ‘Stereo’.

[6] [5]
Catalogue
SAPM 198 009/012 (first stereo edition, four LPs); the scanned export pressing carries ARC 73 125–⁠73 128 / SAPM 198 625–⁠628 Documented

First release year is disputed in the sources: the booklet and Wikipedia say 1959 (the booklet reads ‘LPs released/veröffentlicht/paru 1959’ and prints ℗ 1959 Deutsche Grammophon); Discogs and the Internet Archive LP catalogue give 1958, which is the recording year. Both dates precede 1963. The digital file used here is a later remaster, not the LP.

[5] [7] [6]
Matrix, take, sides
First stereo edition: first programme side of the set (Discogs side A), first track (9:50 on the LP); matrix and take numbers not read Documented

The side and position come from the Discogs tracklist only, whose first edition is automatically coupled, so the programme side is not the physical side of a particular LP. No run-out inscription was seen, so matrix and take are unknown.

[5]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No remastering engineer or studio is credited in the item metadata or the booklet. The booklet’s © 2001 Deutsche Grammophon notice and the retail page’s ‘Digitally remastered’ line show only that commercial digital releases exist. The upload is a private Internet Archive upload in the hifidelity collection.

[1] [4]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is established. The Internet Archive item was created on 16 February 2026; that upload date is not a transfer date.

Processing
24-bit/192 kHz FLAC (item description ‘1959 [FLAC 24-192]’), digitally remastered according to the retail page; streamed here through the Internet Archive’s VBR MP3 derivative. Inferred, not documented

The item’s track titles and durations (9:49 for this track) match the retail page’s 2016 hi-res listing, so the file is probably that release, but the item names no source. No speed correction, noise reduction or restoration settings are stated.

[1] [2] [4]
Composition rights
Bach’s composition (d. 1750) and the Bach-⁠Gesellschaft edition used for the orchestra view (Breitkopf & Härtel, 1854) are public domain. Documented

IMSLP catalogues the Bach-⁠Gesellschaft volume as Public Domain. This does not clear the sound recording, the later remaster or the booklet’s prose.

[8]
Recording rights
territorial — European recording-rights expiry; first publication documented before 1963 (Archiv Produktion stereo LP edition, 1958 or 1959). Documented

Programme rule 3. The recording was made in June–August 1958 and first issued on four stereo LPs; the booklet states 1959 and quotes a critic’s review of the four LPs from May 1959. Whether the first issue fell in 1958 or 1959, a recording published by 1959 had exhausted the ordinary EU 50-year phonogram term (to the end of 2009) before the extension that applied from 1 November 2013. This is territorial, not a licence: the Internet Archive item carries no licence URL and no Public Domain Mark. US status is not established and no US public-domain claim is made. The audio file is a later commercial digital remaster; this dossier relies on the first publication of the recording and does not separately clear any rights claimed in the remastering, which is a point for the integration lead.

[3] [5] [7] [6] [1]

J. S. Bach, St Matthew Passion, BWV 244: No. 1, Kommt, ihr Töchter, helft mir klagen. Münchener Bach-⁠Chor, Münchener Chorknaben, Münchener Bach-⁠Orchester; Karl Richter. Recorded June–August 1958, Herkulessaal, Munich. Archiv Produktion SAPM 198 009/012, first issued 1958–⁠59. Digital remaster via the Internet Archive. European recording-rights expiry only; US status unestablished. Rights statement
